section_1.title: The Intuitive Hook: The Prism Analogy
section_1.content: Introduce the Fourier Transform as a tool that decomposes a complex signal into its constituent simple frequencies, analogous to a prism splitting white light into a rainbow spectrum.
section_1.example: Visualizing a 'smoothie' made of fruit (the signal) being separated back into individual berries (the frequencies).

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Language of Waves
section_2.content: Briefly define a periodic function using sine and cosine waves. Explain the concept of the 'Domain' shift: moving from Time Domain (what happens when?) to Frequency Domain (what is it made of?).
section_2.example: An animation showing a clock ticking (time) vs. the pitch of the ticking sound (frequency).

section_3.title: The Core Mechanism: The Rotating Phasor
section_3.content: Explain Euler's formula visually. Imagine a point tracing a circle; when viewed from the side, it creates a sine wave. The Fourier Transform essentially 'spins' the signal at different frequencies to see if it resonates.
section_3.example: A spinning arm of a robot capturing a signal; when the arm's rotation speed matches the signal's frequency, the center of mass shifts, indicating a 'match'.

section_4.title: The Mathematical Blueprint
section_4.content: Present the integral equation $F(ω) = ∫ f(t)e^{-iωt} dt$. Break it down: the multiplication with the complex exponential acts as a filter that picks out components matching frequency ω.
section_4.example: A 'sieve' metaphor: the integral is a sieve that only lets grains of a specific size (frequency) pass through.

section_5.title: Real-world Application: Noise Cancellation
section_5.content: Demonstrate how the Fourier Transform identifies unwanted noise frequencies in an audio signal, allowing the system to subtract them and leave only the music.
section_5.example: A noisy recording of a bird chirping near a highway; the Fourier Transform isolates the high-pitch chirp from the low-frequency drone of cars.
